page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 64 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes 32 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% of evaluated instances. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory performance is a notable strength, with PassMark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, supported by a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 553.05 GB/sec. Cryptographic and vector operations are supported via hardware-accelerated instructions such as AES, VAES, and AVX.

This instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. Typical applications include database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-heavy web serving. While it handles smaller language model inference tasks adequately, performance drops significantly on larger models, as evidenced by weak prompt processing speeds on 7B parameter models. The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density for memory-bound applications, presenting a qualitative cost-efficient alternative to standard compute instances when memory capacity is the primary constraint.
